content.comment_body: Hello everyone, what is the distinction between transistor and relay outputs for [product_name] PLCs? In which scenarios should transistor outputs be used, and when are relay outputs preferable?

Hi, briefly: transistor outputs handle up to 0.3A and relay outputs up to 10A. That's a primary difference. Transistor outputs are suitable for small loads like 24V (or 12V), while relay outputs are for heavier loads or when you need potential-free switching. Consult the [product_name] manual for detailed technical data. Best regards, [user_name]
So, I can use transistor outputs to activate relay coils directly, or use the PLC's relay outputs as needed.

Correct—if you have small relay coils operating at the same voltage as your [product_name], typically 24VDC, it's possible. Relay outputs feature free contacts and can work with voltages between 3V–250V AC or DC. Transistor outputs operate silently and without moving parts, making them better for frequent switching. Relay outputs always make a slight clicking sound when they switch on or off.

Hi, that's accurate. Personally, I prefer external relays instead of the relay version of the PLC—it’s easier to replace a small interface relay than the relay in the PLC itself. If space is limited, the relay version might be worth considering. Regards, [user_name]
Thank you, your explanation was very helpful. Best regards, [user_name]

Regarding your query, consider using transistor outputs for high-frequency switching, above what a relay can tolerate. Transistor outputs (solid state) support fast rates, contrary to relays which are slower due to their electromechanical nature. If you need to switch higher currents, you can use a solid-state relay with transistor outputs. Also, depending on max frequency, transistor outputs may drive servos or stepper motors. Different PLC series have varied capabilities.

Relays in the 12/24RC unit are rated at 10A, but at what voltage? Is it 24V max at 10A? Can the relay handle AC voltage too? If so, what are the specs for 230V and its maximum current? I couldn't find these details in the manual. Thanks!
It's stated in the manual, though perhaps not very clearly. Relay specs for the 230V version are the same. Maximum load depends on type. Please see the attached specifications. Regards, [user_name]
[user_name], thank you! So it's safe to connect a contactor coil to 220V—appreciate the info.
A new question from [user_name] has been moved to a different thread titled: Choosing [product_name] outputs for heating device. Best regards, [user_name]

Transistors are solid-state electronic switches with a max current of 300mA for [product_name] outputs; relays are electromagnetic switches suited for higher currents, such as 4A. For applications needing pulse or PWM switching, transistor outputs are preferable.
There are other output types available as well, such as optoTRIAC and optoDIAC.
I believe the PLC uses triac technology for its outputs.
